name: Zeek Fundamentals — Architecture, Logs & zeek-cut
description: Zeek (formerly Bro) is a network traffic analyzer for passive analysis, logging, and scripting-based detection. Architecture: event engine (packets → high-level events) + script interpreter (events → actions via Zeek scripts). Key logs: conn.log, dns.log, http.log, ftp.log, smtp.log, smb_files.log, dce_rpc.log. zeek-cut extracts specific columns from TSV logs. Older logs are gzip-compressed hourly into YYYY-MM-DD directories.
notes:
=== ZEEK OVERVIEW ===
Zeek is NOT a signature-based IDS — it's a semantic analysis platform:
  → Semantic misuse detection
  → Anomaly detection
  → Behavioral analysis
  → Full application-layer protocol decoding
  → Generates structured TSV logs for all observed traffic

Zeek analyzes application-layer protocols regardless of port number.

=== OPERATION MODES ===
  Fully passive traffic analysis
  libpcap interface for packet capture
  Real-time and offline (PCAP-based) analysis
  Cluster support for large-scale deployments

=== ARCHITECTURE ===
1. Event Engine (Core):
   → Converts raw packet stream into high-level events
   → Events are policy-neutral (describe WHAT happened, not if it's bad)
   → Example: HTTP request → http_request event (all details, no judgment)
   → Events queued and processed first-come, first-served
   → Most events defined in .bif files at:
     /scripts/base/bif/plugins/
   → Event reference: https://docs.zeek.org/en/stable/scripts/base/bif/

2. Script Interpreter:
   → Executes Zeek scripts (event handlers written in Zeek's scripting language)
   → Scripts express the 'site security policy'
   → Scripts define what to DO when certain events are detected
   → Similar in concept to Suricata rules but much more powerful (Turing complete)

=== RUNNING ZEEK ===
Offline PCAP analysis:
  /usr/local/zeek/bin/zeek -C -r /home/htb-student/pcaps/suspicious.pcap
    → -C: ignore checksum errors
    → -r: read from PCAP file
    → Logs written to current directory

Live analysis:
  /usr/local/zeek/bin/zeek -i ens160
    → Live capture on interface

Download PCAP from target for local analysis:
  scp htb-student@<TARGET_IP>:/home/htb-student/pcaps/psempire.pcap .

=== KEY LOG FILES ===
conn.log:
  → All IP/TCP/UDP/ICMP connections
  → Fields: ts, uid, id.orig_h, id.orig_p, id.resp_h, id.resp_p,
             proto, service, duration, orig_bytes, resp_bytes, conn_state,
             history, orig_pkts, orig_ip_bytes, resp_pkts, resp_ip_bytes
  → Use for: traffic volume analysis, beaconing detection, connection patterns

dns.log:
  → All DNS queries and responses
  → Fields: ts, uid, id.orig_h, id.resp_h, query, qtype, qtype_name,
             rcode, rcode_name, answers, TTLs
  → Use for: DNS enumeration, tunneling, DGA detection

http.log:
  → HTTP requests and responses
  → Fields: host (domain/IP), uri, referrer, user_agent, status_code
  → Use for: web activity, C2 beaconing, file downloads

ftp.log:
  → FTP requests and responses

smtp.log:
  → SMTP transactions (sender, recipient, subject)

smb_files.log:
  → SMB file operations (open, write, delete)
  → Key for PsExec detection (PSEXESVC.exe on ADMIN$)

dce_rpc.log:
  → DCE/RPC calls over named pipes
  → Key for PsExec (svcctl: CreateServiceW, StartServiceW, DeleteService)

smb_mapping.log:
  → SMB share mappings (\\host\ADMIN$, \\host\IPC$)

files.log:
  → Files extracted from network traffic

ssl.log:
  → TLS/SSL session metadata

=== ZEEK-CUT UTILITY ===
zeek-cut: extracts specific columns from Zeek TSV logs
  → Reads from stdin (pipe logs into it)
  → Outputs only specified column(s)

Syntax:
  cat conn.log | /usr/local/zeek/bin/zeek-cut <field1> <field2> ...

Examples:
  # Extract query field from dns.log:
  cat dns.log | /usr/local/zeek/bin/zeek-cut query | cut -d . -f1-7

  # Sum bytes per src/dst pair (TLS exfil detection):
  cat conn.log | /usr/local/zeek/bin/zeek-cut id.orig_h id.resp_h orig_bytes \
    | sort | grep -v -e '^$' | grep -v '-' \
    | datamash -g 1,2 sum 3 | sort -k 3 -rn | head -10
    → datamash -g 1,2: group by columns 1+2 (src+dst IPs)
    → sum 3: sum column 3 (orig_bytes)
    → sort -k 3 -rn: sort by bytes descending
    → Reveals top talkers / exfil destinations

=== LOG COMPRESSION ===
Zeek compresses logs hourly by default:
  → Older logs: gzip compressed
  → Moved to YYYY-MM-DD/ directory

Working with compressed logs:
  gzcat log.gz          → print gzipped log
  zgrep 'pattern' *.gz  → search within gzipped logs

Reference: https://docs.zeek.org/en/master/logs/index.html

=== CONN_STATE VALUES ===
SF  → normal established + closed connection
S0  → connection attempt seen, no reply
S1  → connection established, not closed
RST → connection reset
REJ → connection rejected

=== ZEEK KEY FEATURES ===
  Comprehensive logging of all network activity
  Application-layer protocol analysis (regardless of port)
  File content inspection across protocols
  IPv6 support
  Tunnel detection and analysis
  Protocol sanity checking
  IDS-like pattern matching
  Powerful domain-aware scripting language
  Outputs structured ASCII TSV logs (or ElasticSearch/DataSeries)
  Real-time external input integration
  External C library for sharing events with other programs
